answer:
**Answer**

Cardinal Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli (the future Pope John XXIII) left the city of **Venice**—the same city where the painter **Titian (Tiziano Vecellio)**, who painted *The Bacchanal of the Andrians*, died—in order to attend the **papal conclave in Rome**.

* After the death of Pope Pius XII (20 July 1958) the College of Cardinals convened in Rome to elect his successor.
* Roncalli, who had been appointed Patriarch of Venice in 1953 and was one of the cardinals eligible to vote, was summoned to Rome.
* On **12 October 1958** he departed Venice by train, hoping to return home after the conclave was concluded. (Later, he was elected Pope.)

So his departure was motivated not by personal or political reasons, but by his role as a cardinal electing the new pope—the conclave required the presence of all cardinals, and Venice was the place where Titian died.

VENICE, October 12, 1958 AD — Cardinal Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli, the Patriarch of Venice and the future Saint John XXIII, left the city by train for Rome today. A large crowd of Venetians went with him to the station. He is seventy-six, and he expects to be back at his work here once the cardinals have chosen a new Pope.

**Answer**

Cardinal Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli (the future Pope John XXIII) left the city of **Venice**—the same city where the painter **Titian (Tiziano Vecellio)**, who painted *The Bacchanal of the Andrians*, died—in order to attend the **papal conclave in Rome**.

* After the death of Pope Pius XII (20 July 1958) the College of Cardinals convened in Rome to elect his successor.
* Roncalli, who had been appointed Patriarch of Venice in 1953 and was one of the cardinals eligible to vote, was summoned to Rome.
* On **12 October 1958** he departed Venice by train, hoping to return home after the conclave was concluded. (Later, he was elected Pope.)

So his departure was motivated not by personal or political reasons, but by his role as a cardinal electing the new pope—the conclave required the presence of all cardinals, and Venice was the place where Titian died.
